subject: dartr 1.9.9.1 on CRAN has a bug with lat lon

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: dartr 1.9.9.1 on CRAN has a bug with lat lon
parts:
Hi everyone,

we just noticed (thanks Renee) that the latest CRAN version has a "severe" bug, if you want to work with lat lon coordinates [good old latlong / latlon confusion].

We bascially tried to rectify the old legacy spelling but introduced an error (read more details below).  In a nut-shell. If you want to have a working gl.map.interactive or also gl2shp and a new gl.ibd then you need to do the following

install the CRAN version
install.packages("dartR")  #CRAN version 1.9.9.1 if you do not have it already

library(dartR) 
packageVersion("dartR") #should be 1.9.9.1

#update to the dev version on Github
gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "dev")
packageVersion("dartR") #should be 1.9.9.7 now
which installs the current dev version on your system.

This has unfortunately the other repercussion that not all new functions are fully tested and we did quite a few changes. We wanted to wait for this until we have consolidated, but the latlong bug on CRAN is severe enough to risk it. So if you have problems with gl.map.interactive you might try to install the dev version.

If this does not work for you you can go back to 1.9.9.1 using
install.packages("dartR")


For a more detailed explanation:
The new lat lon naming is now more consistent. The coordinates are stored now under

gl@other$latlon [not long anymore].

The good news is that the system is backward compatible so if you have older genlight object that sill use @other$latlong the new function work or you can use

glnew <- gl.compliance.check(gl)
to rename the coordinates to the correct latlon slot.

new gl.ibd (isolation by distance analysis).
This function has now received a new overhaul. It allows to calculate several pairwise distances (individuals based and population based) and also any transformation of the genetic and geographic distances. As a new feature you can now also plot an pairwise individual distances (so 1-proportionofshared alleles) but color the dots by the population identity of individuals. A example for bandicoots.gl is obtained via:

gl.ibd(bandicoots.gl, distance="propShared", pairscol="pop", Dgeo_trans="log(Dgeo)")

It also projects now coordinates from lat lon s, runs the mantel test and returns the coefficients, or the fitted line (might be interesting in some cases).

Sorry for the inconvenience,

Cheers, Bernd
